              Justin Devenny on 'loving' life at Stoke, promotion ambitions and Michael O'Neill talks

              Justin Devenny has taken time to get going at Stoke City following his summer move from Crystal Palace but the midfielder is now full of confidence after the 1-0 win against Birmingham City

              Comments0
              Sport
              Daniel Orme Midlands Football Reporter
              13:15, 23 Nov 2026Updated 13:17, 23 Nov 2026
              Listen to audio version of this article
              Sponsored by
              0:00 / 3:51
              Instaread

              Justin Devenny is resisting the temptation to look at the Championship table - but promotion remains on his mind.

              ‌
              ‌

              Devenny, 23, joined the Potters from Crystal Palace in the summer and has already had quite an impact in Staffordshire.

              ‌

              After scoring twice on his debut against Charlton Athletic, his performances have helped Stoke to the lofty heights of second in the Championship - a position that he is determined to help the club keep a hold of.

              ‌

              Speaking after Saturday’s memorable win against Birmingham City, he said: “I think my main target when I signed here was to get promoted. I think that’s always got to be in your head and I think that was always in my head coming from the Premier League, you just want to get back there.

              11 players could miss Stoke City vs Millwall after Djibril Soumare and Luca Bombino blows

              Met Office names Staffordshire in latest snow forecast

              Make sure you never miss the latest Stoke City news and opinion by making The Sentinel one of your Google preferred sources

              “It’s important to set yourself goals as well. When I signed, I obviously spoke to the manager and I think everyone was in the same boat.

              ‌
              Sign up to FREE email alerts from Stoke City news

              We use your sign-up to provide content in ways you've consented to and improve our understanding of you. This may include adverts from us and third parties based on our knowledge of you. More info

              “It’s an ambitious club with ambitious players and it’s ambitious for me to want to get back up there because Stoke have had a long history in the Premier League and it’s up to us to get back up there.

              “I’m loving it, I love it here. Getting minutes and showcase my talent and stuff is what I’ve missed out on over the past few years with the consistency so I think it’s obviously great being here. It’s such a good group to be part of.”

              ‌

              And despite excitement building in the Potteries, as evidenced by the biggest home crowd of the season against Birmingham, Devenny says no one is getting carried away quite yet.

              ‌

              He added: “You always know what’s going on but for me personally, I don’t look at it really. I know when you’re winning, everyone else is winning around you anyway.

              “It’s always tight, it’s always close. You just need to look at the controllables and not look too far ahead.

              ‌

              “I think we all know as a group that there’s a long way to go and you see that season upon season. When it comes to this time of year, whoever is at the top is not necessarily there.

              “For us, we can’t be getting carried away. We’ve just got to keep doing what we’re doing. Hopefully that will take us up there.”

              ‌

              Devenny arrived in the Potteries from Crystal Palace late in the summer transfer window, signing a four-year deal with Stoke.

              ‌

              And the midfielder has since revealed that both current midfielder Ethan Galbraith, as well as former manager Michael O’Neill - who is now in charge of Northern Ireland - backed the move.

              Devenny said. “I spoke to two people, it was Michael O’Neill and Ethan Galbraith and at the same time, everyone was saying it was such a massive club.

              ‌

              “I probably had a good hour conversation with Michael and he was telling me how it was a massive club and how it was run.

              “He said to me he thinks it’s a really good match because he thinks they’ll be able to get the best out of me and hopefully throughout the season, you’ll see that. So it was all positive on that side of things.”
